title: Reset GAUL to UN Geodata 2023
summary: GAUL's polygons and lines date from the 2018 UN Geodata, so they are reset to the 2023 versions. Each border that changed since 2018 is listed with the land between the two lines.

title: Fix likely UN Geodata errors
summary: These look like errors in UN Geodata 2023, so both exports correct them.

title: Representation of disputed and dependent areas
summary: UN Geodata and GAUL draw some disputed and dependent areas differently. UN Geodata covers them with lines inside a neighbouring country or a larger disputed area, and GAUL gives each one its own polygon. Here, the UN export follows UN Geodata and the GAUL export follows GAUL, until the two agree.

title: Reset coastlines to OSM
summary: For information. Both exports take OSM's coastline. Each entity gains the land OSM draws beyond UN Geodata's coast, loses the land OSM draws as water (such as the Caspian sectors) and drops UN Geodata land that touches no OSM land. OSM islands with no UN Geodata land go to the entity whose cell holds them, where FieldMaps agrees. No land changes owner.

title: Owners of new islands
summary: OSM islands with no UN Geodata land whose owner is open: FieldMaps' cell gives them to another entity, or a line between two cells crosses them. Each goes to the entity whose cell holds them and is listed for review. Minerva Reefs, disputed between Fiji and Tonga, get their own entity.
